key_insight: QuFrame is a quantum-control microarchitecture designed to track Pauli frames in real time and close the quantum error-correction loop within 1 μs.
engineering_relevance: It addresses the real-time control dependencies introduced by non-Clifford gates, where error-corrected measurements must guide ongoing execution.
method: QuFrameISA separates instruction execution from continuous Pauli frame management.
Per-qubit Instruction Resolution Engines use a single table lookup, while a Pauli Frame Management Unit supports lock-free concurrent commits.
An asynchronous primary decoder is paired with an on-chip fallback decoder, with hardware reconciliation of divergent updates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 144 ns fallback decoding, QPU-rate throughput, and a 1 μs QEC loop without degraded logical error rates, but gives no evaluation setup.
watch_item: The abstract leaves hardware resource costs and scaling across large distributed control systems unspecified.
paper_title: QuFrame: Pauli Frame Tracking for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Control
